t: Heir to the army and the Greek alliance built by his father Philip II, Alexander became king of Macedon at 20 and in ten years of campaigning from 334 BCE overthrew the Achaemenid Persian Empire.

The conquests were made with massacres and enslavement at Thebes, Tyre, Gaza and Massaga, and his adoption of Persian customs and the killing of his own officers cost him the sympathy of many Macedonians.

He died at Babylon at 32 without an obvious heir; his generals fought for forty years over an empire that broke into Hellenistic kingdoms, through which Greek language and culture spread from Egypt to India.
dyk: Alexander's body was laid in a gold sarcophagus filled with honey. His companion Ptolemy seized the funeral cortege on its way to Macedon and took the body to Egypt, where a later king, Ptolemy IX Lathyros, replaced the gold sarcophagus with a glass one so that he could turn the original into coin.
ev: Alexander is born at Pella, the capital of Macedon, to King Philip II and Olympias
Philip II is assassinated at Aigai and Alexander is proclaimed king by the nobles and army at the age of 20
After a campaign in the Balkans he razes rebellious Thebes and divides its territory among the other Boeotian cities
His army crosses the Hellespont into Asia and defeats Persian forces at the Battle of the Granicus
He defeats Darius III at Issus; Darius flees, leaving behind his wife, daughters and mother
Victory over Darius at Gaugamela, the final and decisive encounter between the two, is followed by the capture of Babylon
He defeats King Porus at the Battle of the Hydaspes in the Punjab, and his army mutinies at the Hyphasis, refusing to march farther east
Alexander dies at Babylon, aged 32, while planning an invasion of Arabia

f.born: Probably 20 July 356 BCE (the exact date is uncertain) at Pella, capital of Macedon; son of King Philip II of the Argead dynasty and his fourth wife, Olympias of Epirus
f.died: 10 or 11 June 323 BCE in the palace of Nebuchadnezzar II at Babylon, aged 32, after an illness of about twelve days; the ancient accounts differ on its course, and some alleged poison
f.role: King of Macedon, 336–323 BCE; Hegemon of the League of Corinth and commander of the war against Persia from 336 BCE; crowned in the temple of Ptah at Memphis in Egypt; ruler of the conquered Achaemenid Empire
f.known: the conquest of the Achaemenid Persian Empire; the battles of Issus, Gaugamela and the Hydaspes; never losing a battle; founding Alexandria in Egypt and more than twenty other cities; the spread of Greek language and culture and the beginning of the Hellenistic period; the legends gathered in the Alexander Romance
